description:
Found while writing fz-kdt.130's fixtures. Not specific to `receive` -- every
`->` arm body has it, so it is a parser fact, not a mailbox one.

    fn main() do
      x = 1
      case x do
        1 ->
          a = 10
          dbg(a)
        _ -> dbg(0)
      end
    end

  error[parse/expected-token]: expected `->`, got Newline

The arm body is parsed as a single expression, so the newline after the first
statement is read as the end of the arm and the parser then demands the next
arm's `->`. Elixir accepts a statement sequence in an arm body. The workaround
in every fixture today is to bind the arm's value out and continue after the
`case`/`receive`, which is why the corpus never exercised it.

Consequence for testing: a claim whose shape is "several things happen inside
one arm" cannot be written directly. fz-kdt.130's fixture had to be restructured
around it.
title: P3: a case/receive arm body parses as one expression, so a multi-statement arm is a parse error
